review_notes: Source is correctly a project-level load point (leptonica pixReadMemTiff / fopenTiffMemstream, tiffio.c:2561), not the fuzz harness entry (LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput/pixReadMem), which is properly relegated to reachability_checkpoints.raw_entry.

Sink (TIFFYCbCrtoRGB tif_color.c:188), store origin (OJPEGDecodeRaw tif_ojpeg.c:847), and uninitialized-heap allocation origin (OJPEGWriteHeaderInfo _TIFFmalloc tif_ojpeg.c:1199) all match the MSAN trace's use/store/alloc stacks exactly.
root_cause anchor (tiffSeekCallback SEEK_SET 'mstream->offset = offset;') and patch_predicate ('if((size_t)offset != offset) return ERROR') match the src/tiffio.c hunk of commit 41a6412 verbatim.

GT correctly attributes the sibling tiffReadCallback overflow guard ('mstream->offset + amount < amount') to the companion heap-overflow issue 14773 rather than to this uninitialized-value path (15269), consistent with the commit message describing two distinct fixes.

fine_trace is a genuine data/control-flow trace (source -> alloc -> root_cause seek -> bounds_state read-callback bailout -> uninitialized store -> propagate -> sink), not a call stack, and includes the class-relevant steps for a CWE-457-rooted-in-integer/size-overflow bug (the offset assignment/size arithmetic AND the downstream memory op and use).

JUDGMENT-CALL FOR STAGE 05 (does not fail static review): the cited patch predicate '(size_t)offset != offset' is a 32-bit-size_t truncation guard, but this repro ran on 64-bit linux/amd64 where size_t==toff_t==64-bit, so that specific seek guard cannot fire for this input. The observed stderr ('Bad file: amount too big: 296004', value fits in 32 bits) shows the vulnerable tiffReadCallback 'offset+amount > hw' check already returned 0 on this 64-bit run. Runtime validation should confirm which of the two commit hunks actually gates the crash on the 64-bit reproducer, since on 64-bit the seek-callback guard is a no-op and the crash-preventing edge may instead be the read-callback change. The GT already acknowledges this configuration dependency and the patch does attribute the size_t fix to issue 15269, so the root_cause anchor remains patch-supported; this is flagged only so 04/05 witness the actual gating condition rather than assuming the 32-bit path.
